'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israeli attacks on Yemen (May 2025–present)|Israeli attacks on Yemen]], [[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[September 2025 Israeli attacks in Yemen]]
***The casualty toll from yesterday's [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]]s in [[Sanaa]] and [[Al Jawf Governorate]], [[Yemen]], increases to 46 people killed and 165 others injured. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/death-toll-rises-46-israeli-raids-yemen-2025-09-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Punjab, Pakistan floods]]
**At least nine people are killed when a [[Lifeboat (rescue)|lifeboat]] carrying flood evacuees capsizes near [[Multan]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], [[Pakistan]], while 15 others are safely rescued. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/boat-capsizes-pakistan-floods-killing-nine-authorities-say-2025-09-12/ (Reuters)]
*At least 107 people are killed and 146 remain missing after a [[whaleboat]] catches fire on the [[Congo River]] near [[Lukolela]], [[Équateur Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], with over 200 survivors rescued. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-107-killed-congo-whaleboat-sinks-river-2025-09-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2025 Kasaï Province Ebola outbreak]]
**An [[Ebola]] outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo doubles in cases as the [[virus]] spreads to more districts in [[Kasai province]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-ebola-kasai-outbreak-b4dfd340373d2f5e4ce2ce40b1eba6e0 (AP)]
*[[Renewable energy in Brazil]]
**[[Clean energy]] [[think tank]] [[Ember (non-profit organisation)|Ember]] reports that [[Wind power|wind]] and [[Solar power in Brazil|solar]] power generated over one-third of [[Brazil]]'s [[Energy in Brazil|electricity]] for the first time in August. [https://apnews.com/article/brazil-wind-solar-power-electricity-renewable-energy-13eef596389803e8b801f26e7888fb97 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–United States relations]]
**[[Belarus]] releases 52 [[Political prisoners in Belarus|political prisoners]], including 14 foreign nationals, following negotiations with the [[United States]]. [https://apnews.com/article/belarus-prisoners-us-lithuania-c217e9bb36b9303e0fa2acd8e0492b37 (AP)]
**Following the release of political prisoners, the U.S. lifts its [[List of people and organizations sanctioned in relation to human rights violations in Belarus|sanctions]] on Belarusian [[flag carrier]] [[Belavia]]. [https://eng.belta.by/president/view/usa-lifts-sanctions-from-belarus-belavia-airline-171373-2025/ (BelTA)]
*[[Belarus–Poland relations]]
**[[Poland]] indefinitely closes its [[Belarus-Poland border|border with Belarus]] and deploys 40,000 troops to it, citing security concerns over [[Zapad 2025|Russian–Belarusian military exercises]] near the region, the first ones since 2022. [https://mezha.net/eng/bukvy/poland-deploys-40-000-troops-near-belarus-and-russia-borders-amid-rising-tensions/ (Mezha)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/poland-close-belarus-border-due-russia-led-military-exercises-pm-says-2025-09-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[Foreign relations of Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Foreign relations of Slovenia]]
**[[Slovenia]] bars [[Bosnian Serb]] [[Separatism|separatist]] leader [[Milorad Dodik]] from entering the country after he refuses to acknowledge his removal as the [[President of Republika Srpska|president]] of [[Republika Srpska]] by the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnia]]n [[Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina|court]] and [[Central Election Commission of Bosnia and Herzegovina|electoral authority]]. [https://apnews.com/article/slovenia-bosnia-dodik-sanctions-b028e5ede51c69dad7d82c086a9a097e (AP)]
*[[Saudi Arabia–Syria relations]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] announces it will supply [[Syria]] with 1.65 million barrels of [[crude oil]] to support the country's rebuilding efforts following the [[Fall of the Assad regime|regime change]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-saudi-crude-oil-d923ae1c8488ccdd7b2f921d60a788ce (AP)]
*[[September 2025 Russian drone incursion into Poland]], [[Poland–Russia relations]]
**[[PANSA]] imposes a three-month [[Prohibited airspace|flight ban]] over the [[Eastern Poland|eastern Polish]] [[airspace]] following the incursion. [https://www.newsweek.com/poland-nato-russia-drones-2128073 (''Newsweek'')]
*[[United Kingdom–United States relations]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] dismisses its [[List of ambassadors of the United Kingdom to the United States|ambassador to the United States]] [[Peter Mandelson]] after newly released emails reveal a closer relationship with [[Americans|American]] [[child sex offender]] [[Jeffrey Epstein]] than previously acknowledged. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/11/uk-fires-ambassador-to-us-peter-mandelson-over-links-to-epstein (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2022 Brazilian coup plot]]
**''[[AP 2668]]''
***The [[Brazil]]ian [[Supreme Federal Court]] convicts former [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] of [[criminal conspiracy|plotting]] a [[coup]] in 2022 after he lost the [[2022 Brazilian presidential election|election]] to [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva|Lula]] and imposes a 27-year prison sentence. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/11/world/americas/brazil-supreme-court-bolsonaro-coup-convict.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.npr.org/2025/09/11/nx-s1-5535658/bolsonaro-brazil-coup-trial (NPR)] [https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/justica/noticia/2025-09/stf-condena-bolsonaro-27-anos-e-tres-meses-de-prisao (Agência Brasil)]
*[[2025 Nasir clashes]]
**A [[Judiciary of South Sudan|court]] in [[South Sudan]] charges [[Vice President of South Sudan|Vice President]] [[Riek Machar]] with [[murder]], [[treason]], and [[crimes against humanity]] in an alleged link to a [[Nuer White Army]] attack in March. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c07vkln2ezro (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Georgian local elections]]
**The [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] [[State Security Service of Georgia|State Security Service]] arrests [[Parliament of Georgia|MP]] [[Levan Khabeishvili]], a leader of the [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] [[United National Movement]], days after he called for a "peaceful revolution" ahead of upcoming elections. [https://www.reuters.com/world/georgia-arrests-opposition-figure-who-urged-peaceful-revolution-polls-2025-09-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines (2024–2025)|Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines]]
**[[Philippines|Philippine]] [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] creates an independent commission with broad investigative powers to examine alleged [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] in [[flood control]] and other infrastructure projects. [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/philippines-forms-independent-body-probe-anomalies-infrastructure-projects-2025-09-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of Albania]], [[Corruption in Albania]], [[Cyberocracy]]
**[[Albania]] appoints an [[Artificial intelligence|AI]] bot named "[[Diella (AI system)|Diella]]" as Minister of Public Procurement, in an effort to increase [[Transparency (behavior)|transparency]] and reduce [[corruption]] in state contracts. This marks the first time a [[Minister (government)|ministerial]] role has been given to an AI system. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2566250/albania-names-ai-bot-as-minister-to-oversee-procurement-fight-corruption (''Tribune'')]
